title: Graph Builder: real measurements, live filters and an explicit handoff limit
description: Drag actual measurement columns into graphs, split by acquisition metadata, filter reversibly and recognize the current annotation-selection defect.
objectives: Load the real example database and choose the cell table.
Build a histogram, scatter plot, colour grouping and row facets.
Verify changing populations while filtering and restoring the chart.
Distinguish internal brush publication from a working annotation handoff.
prerequisite: Download and unzip the linked real measurement database, or use the downloaded Annotate example. The archive contains measurements, not image crops; no new model run is needed.

scenes.narration: Graph Builder explores an existing table. Open it from Home; this is a main module, with Plate Viewer and Small Multiples nested inside it. We will use actual example measurements, not train a model or ask an AI service to generate results.

Choose Load table and open measurements dot db from the linked archive or the downloaded Annotate example. Select the cell table: two thousand three hundred forty-one rows. The archive preserves the recorded database exactly. It does not include the images referenced by other tables.

Search for cell_area and drag that column onto X. Automatic plotting makes a thirty-bin histogram. Each bar counts cell rows in an area interval; it is not a treatment comparison or a significance test. The values retain their stored units, without new physical calibration.

Drag cell_channel_1_mean_intensity onto Y. Now each point represents a cell's area and channel-one mean intensity. Overlapping points can hide one another visually, although all rows are represented here. Inspect the row-count notice; larger datasets may use a different drawing policy.

Put columnID on Colour and read the legend. The colours distinguish acquisition columns, not inferred classes or known treatments. A visual separation is descriptive evidence to investigate, not proof of an effect. We checked the plotted coordinates and colour assignments against the source rows.

Put rowID on the downward facet channel to split the chart into plate-row panels. Their counts are one thousand one hundred forty and one thousand two hundred one. Shared axes help comparison, but cells within a well are not independent experimental replicates.

In the right-hand filter panel, add cell_area and set its minimum to twenty-one thousand nine hundred twenty-five. The chart updates immediately to one thousand one hundred seventy-one rows. This rounded median illustrates the filter; it is not a recommended biological threshold. Notice that the axis limits also change.

Choose Clear all in the filter panel to restore all two thousand three hundred forty-one cells. This is different from Clear all channels on the left, which removes plot mappings. Recheck the count and axes after filtering; a changed population is not a new measurement.

Remove the row facet with its small cross, then drag a rectangle on the scatter. This build has a defect: the recorded gesture publishes six hundred fifty-three object keys internally, but shows zero selected and leaves Open selection in Annotate disabled. Do not assume annotations were opened or created.

A plain click clears that internal selection too. The tutorial verifies this recovery but does not repair the handoff. Filtering and pointing at objects are different operations, and other views may share their state. Always check the active population rather than treating a graph as the full database automatically.

Use the header shortcuts for the nested Plate Viewer and Small Multiples workflows; their separate tutorials cover those tools. This screen has no chart or specification export button. The linked database archive is an external tutorial download, not a Graph Builder export.

For Python work, read_table loads the data, GraphSpec describes plot channels and facets, and the selection API distinguishes filters from explicit object keys. Save the source, settings and version with your interpretation. These APIs neither validate a biological conclusion nor fix the annotation handoff.
